D.B. Cooper Hijacking works best when it is read as a shaped story rather than a loose set of notes. D.B. Cooper is the unidentified man who hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 on November 24, 1971, received $200,000 and parachutes, then jumped from the aircraft over the Pacific Northwest. The FBI investigated for decades but closed the case in 2016 without identifying him. The important movement is not only what the tale names, but how its setting, central image, and unresolved pressure make the reader want to keep following it.
